title: Cohomological amplitude of a complex over a DVR is detected modulo the uniformizer
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\varpi$ and residue field $\kappa=R/\varpi R$, and let $D(R)$ be the derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology modules $H^i(-)$. Let $M\in D(R)$ be such that $H^i(M)=0$ for all but finitely many $i$ and every $H^i(M)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. Let $M\otimes^L_R\kappa$ be the derived tensor product, represented by the cone of $\varpi\cdot\operatorname{id}_M:M\to M$ (since $0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi}R\to\kappa\to0$ is a free resolution of $\kappa$). If $a\leq b$ are integers such that $H^i(M\otimes^L_R\kappa)=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$, then $H^i(M)=0$ for every $i\notin[a,b]$.

source.place: proof of Theorem 19.2, p. 125: the exact sequence 0 -> H^r(M)/l^n H^r(M) -> H^r(M_n) -> H^{r+1}(M)_{l^n} -> 0 and 'H^r(M) is generated by any subset that generates it modulo l' (Nakayama); also literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex, Lemma 10.20.1 (Tag 00DV, Nakayama). Hidden in the blueprint proof of prop-cohomological-finiteness, Step 4 ('finitely generated over the Noetherian ring O_E ... with the same vanishing range')

proof.text: Choose a cochain complex representing $M$ and form the cone of multiplication by $\varpi$ on that complex. By the cone model stipulated in the statement and the distinguished-cone-triangle definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this gives a distinguished triangle $M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\to M\otimes_R^L\kappa\to M[1]$. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives the exact segment $H^i(M)\xrightarrow{\varpi}H^i(M)\to H^i(M\otimes_R^L\kappa)\to H^{i+1}(M)\xrightarrow{\varpi}H^{i+1}(M)$. The kernel of the map out of the second term is $\varpi H^i(M)$, so it induces an injection from $H^i(M)/\varpi H^i(M)$ into the third term. Exactness at the third and fourth terms says that its cokernel is $H^{i+1}(M)[\varpi]=\{x:\varpi x=0\}$. Thus $0\to H^i(M)/\varpi H^i(M)\to H^i(M\otimes_R^L\kappa)\to H^{i+1}(M)[\varpi]\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 05RS, lemma-cohomology-homological and equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence-D, for the homotopy category; Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category, for passage to the derived category; Tag 0147, definition-homological and equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence. Milne, proof of Theorem 19.2, p. 125, gives the analogous quotient-torsion sequence.

proof.text: Fix any integer $i\notin[a,b]$. The middle term of the short exact sequence in Step 1 is zero by hypothesis, hence $H^i(M)/\varpi H^i(M)=0$, or equivalently $\varpi H^i(M)=H^i(M)$. By the definition of a DVR and uniformizer [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $R$ is local with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=(\varpi)$. Its Jacobson radical, the intersection of all maximal ideals, is therefore $\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson] with ideal $I=(\varpi)$ and module $N=H^i(M)$: $N$ is finitely generated by hypothesis, $I$ is contained in the Jacobson radical, and $IN=N$. It follows that $H^i(M)=0$. Since $i$ was arbitrary outside $[a,b]$, this proves the asserted bound at both ends.

The statement is true. The cone of multiplication by ϖ is M⊗^Lκ, because 0→R→R→κ→0 is a free resolution (ϖ≠0 in a domain). Small cases behave as expected: κ[0], R[0] and (R/ϖ²)[-3] give the predicted ranges, and Frac(R)[0] shows that the finite-generation hypothesis is needed and it is there. Step 1: the cone triangle comes from the cone clause of def-weil-abstract-derived-category, and lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact gives the long exact sequence. From it, the passage to 0→H^i/ϖ→H^i(cone)→H^{i+1}[ϖ]→0 is elementary and correct. Step 2: def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring gives that R is local with maximal ideal (ϖ), so the Jacobson radical is (ϖ). lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson then applies with all its hypotheses met, matching Stacks 00DV lemma-NAK (2), which I read. I checked Milne LEC Th. 19.2 on p. 125, the Stacks tags 05RS/05RT/05RU/0147 against their labels, and the Mathlib declarations: Nakayama.lean:118, HomologySequence.lean:152-181 and DVR Basic.lean:58. All four cited nodes are Mathlib leaves, so the item makes no route use. The two declared tool_uses are therefore unnecessary, but their content is accurate and I accept them as harmless. The report's line that no exception is requested is slightly inconsistent with them; I left that unchanged. The from.place quotation of blueprint main-20261015 Step 4 is verbatim. Step 7 relies on the same passage, and the reference fits unit sk-lem-finite Step 3. The parent's use (Step 6, a=0, b=2e, C in D^b_fg(O_E)) matches the hypotheses.
